target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` without `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect and previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) is still useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing. Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError` instead, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs are unchanged (`healthy` on connect).

## Evidence

### L1
- Unit: `publishSlackConnectedStatus(..., { degraded: true })` asserts `healthState: "degraded"` and `lastError` in `provider.reconnect.test.ts`.

### L3 live (redacted) — real Slack workspace `hah`

Used live Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-…REDACTED`) and User OAuth Token (`xoxp-…REDACTED`) via local env only (not committed). **Rotate these tokens if they were pasted into chat.**

**BEFORE (old always-healthy on connect):**
```json
{
  "connected": true,
  "healthState": "healthy",
  "lastError": null
}
```

**LIVE `auth.test` with bot token:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "user_id": "U0BFV1X131V",
  "bot_id": "B0BGACNKEGJ",
  "team": "hah"
}
```

**LIVE `auth.test` with user token misused as botToken:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "user_id": "U0BGAB38H7C",
  "bot_id": null,
  "team": "hah"
}
```

**Identity warning (production helper text):**
```
Slack auth.test identified account "default" as user U0BGAB38H7C without bot_id. channels.slack.botToken appears to contain a user token; replace it with a Bot User OAuth Token. Until replaced, explicit bot-mention detection is disabled and required-mention channels fail closed.
```

**AFTER (fixed degraded publish):**
```json
{
  "connected": true,
  "healthState": "degraded",
  "lastError": "Slack auth.test identified account \"default\" as user U0BGAB38H7C without bot_id. channels.slack.botToken appears to contain a user token; replace it with a Bot User OAuth Token. Until replaced, explicit bot-mention detection is disabled and required-mention channels fail closed."
}
```

Note: Full Socket Mode end-to-end status via Gateway also needs an App-Level Token (`xapp-…`); this L3 proves the identity gate + status publisher contract with live `auth.test` against the real workspace.

### Agent Transcript
- Cursor session: Slack L3 live identity/status proof (tokens redacted; rotate if exposed).
